description: A square town quarter cut into irregular lots along streets, centred on the origin (Y up, metres). Voronoi blocks shrunk by half a street leave the streets; each block is cut into lots by a relaxed Voronoi of its own (lots shared out by block area), and every lot gets one house that follows its shape: the lot shrunk to a house 9 to 13 m across (smaller lots keep a strip of garden all round), pushed to 2 m behind the lot's street front, so a front garden, side strips and a back garden stay free. Walls carry a window in every facade cell and a door to the street; a straight-skeleton roof on the footprint is hipped with 0.35 m eaves or pitched with vertical gables on its two ends. About a third of the houses get extra_floors on top. The render (node town_view) shows the three outputs over the lots drawn as gardens.

lots.label: lots
lots.desc: how many lots the quarter is cut into

street_width.label: street width
street_width.desc: width of the streets between the blocks of lots (m)

floors.label: floors
floors.desc: floors of an ordinary house (3 m each)

extra_floors.label: extra floors
extra_floors.desc: floors that about a third of the houses, picked at random, get on top

seed.label: seed
seed.desc: changes the plan, the colours and which houses grow taller

blocks.note: the street plan: about one block per five lots (fewer where the streets would eat a small quarter: no block narrower than about two street widths), each cell shrunk by half a street

plan.note: cut every block into lots: the lots are shared out by block area (at least one each), seeded by best-candidate sampling inside the block, relaxed five times (Lloyd) and clipped to the block, so lots tile each block exactly (corners closer than 1 cm merged). Every lot draws its floors, roof style and colours, and gets its street front (the outward direction of its longest edge on the block's edge; for a lot inside a block, of its edge that faces most away from the block's centre), its yard gap (2 m, less on a tiny lot) and how deep its house reaches from the front (8 to 11 m behind the gap)

footprints.note: every lot shrunk by its yard gap, so a strip of garden stays free along every lot edge; workaround: straight_skeleton offset refuses lots that share an edge, so each lot is offset on its own

house_plan.note: each house fills its lot's garden-strip outline from the street front back to its depth (and at most 22 m along the front), so it follows the lot's front and sides and leaves a back garden; corners sharper than 80° are cut back (up to 1 m), so eaves and roofs stay inside the yard gap; every outline point carries its house's wall height. Workaround: corners closer than 5 cm and straight corners are dropped (the straight-skeleton roof fails on a near-straight corner)

walls.note: one wall quad per outline edge, as high as the house, facing out. Workaround: extrude drops the outline's attributes, so the walls are built here

door_sites.note: one door per house: the middle facade cell of the wall that faces the lot's street front most (on a cell 1.4 m or wider where there is one). Workaround: removeprim with its points would also delete the new door points (no prim uses them), so prims and old points are removed separately

facade_cells.note: every wall cell 1.8 m or wider gets a window, but the door's

eaves.note: hipped roofs reach 0.35 m past the walls (always inside the yard gap); pitched roofs stop flush, so their gables stand on the walls

roof_plan.note: every roof edge slopes at roof_pitch; a pitched roof gets a vertical gable (90°) on the two ends across its longest side, where those ends are 2 m or longer, not next to each other and turned at least 33° from the ridge

roof_slopes.note: the sloped faces get the roof's thickness; the gables stay single faces flush with the walls below (thickening them too folds the shell at their corners)

roof_surfaces.note: the gables are wall, the rest roof tiles

params.code:
const b = primintrinsic(0, 'bounds', @primnum);
s@material = Math.abs(@N[1]) < 0.05 && b[3] - b[2] > 0.4 ? 'plaster_' + @wall : 'roof_' + @tiles;

house_tidy.note: keep lot, name, floors, height and material: the build attributes, the door copy's normals and uvs and the facade groups go

params.names: roof wall tiles fx fz cell_u cell_v edge copynum pitch N uv

house_normals.note: hard edges at every roof ridge, hip and window corner

house_paint.note: Cd follows each prim's material, for viewers and formats that show Cd

params.code:
const table = JSON.parse(detail(0, 'materials') || '{}');
for (let p = 0; p < nprims(0); p++) { const m = table[prim(0, 'material', p)]; if (m) setprimattrib(0, 'Cd', p, m.baseColor); }

house_survey.note: measures the promises on the finished houses against the lot outlines: per lot the houses whose ground centre lies in it, per house whether every point stays inside that lot, and its lowest point

params.names: floors height roof wall tiles gap depth fx fz

street_faces.note: the quarter minus the blocks: half a street wide along the quarter's edge, so quarters tile

yards.note: for the picture only: every lot a garden, in one of three greens so neighbouring lots read apart

town_view.note: the picture: the three outputs over the lots shown as gardens

houses.label: Houses
houses.description: One house per lot, following the lot's shape inside it with garden all round: walls with windows and a door to the street, and a hipped or pitched straight-skeleton roof on the footprint; prims named house_NN after their lot.

lots.label: Lots
lots.description: The outline of every lot as a closed-loop polyline on the ground, named lot_NN (the house on it is house_NN), for gardens, fences or paths.

streets.label: Streets
streets.description: The flat street surface between the blocks of lots, half a street wide along the quarter's edge so quarters can tile.
